claim: TMEM175 is a potassium (K+)-selective cation channel that is evolutionarily distinct from all other known ion channels.
source: Transmembrane protein 175 (TMEM175) is a potassium (K+)-selective cation channel that is evolutionarily distinct from all other known ion channels.
evidence: This is a statement in the introduction that establishes the basic identity and uniqueness of TMEM175.

claim: In mammals, TMEM175 is expressed in lysosomes.
source: In mammals, TMEM175 is expressed in lysosomes, where it is critical for maintaining lysosomal homeostasis (Cang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cang et al., 2015.

claim: TMEM175 is critical for maintaining lysosomal homeostasis.
source: In mammals, TMEM175 is expressed in lysosomes, where it is critical for maintaining lysosomal homeostasis (Cang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cang et al., 2015.

claim: TMEM175 contributes to establishing the membrane potential across the lysosomal membrane.
source: As a K+-selective channel, TMEM175 contributes to establishing the membrane potential across the lysosomal membrane (Cang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cang et al., 2015.

claim: Loss of TMEM175 function can lead to dysregulation of lysosomal pH.
source: Loss of TMEM175 function can lead to numerous defects in the endolysosomal system including dysregulation of lysosomal pH, defects in autophagy and mitophagy, reduced glucocerebrosidase activity, and an increased susceptibility to α-synuclein cytotoxicity (Jinn et al., 2019; Jinn et al., 2017; Krohn et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jinn et al., 2019; Jinn et al., 2017; Krohn et al., 2020.

claim: Loss of TMEM175 function can lead to defects in autophagy and mitophagy.
source: Loss of TMEM175 function can lead to numerous defects in the endolysosomal system including dysregulation of lysosomal pH, defects in autophagy and mitophagy, reduced glucocerebrosidase activity, and an increased susceptibility to α-synuclein cytotoxicity (Jinn et al., 2019; Jinn et al., 2017; Krohn et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jinn et al., 2019; Jinn et al., 2017; Krohn et al., 2020.

claim: Loss of TMEM175 function can lead to reduced glucocerebrosidase activity.
source: Loss of TMEM175 function can lead to numerous defects in the endolysosomal system including dysregulation of lysosomal pH, defects in autophagy and mitophagy, reduced glucocerebrosidase activity, and an increased susceptibility to α-synuclein cytotoxicity (Jinn et al., 2019; Jinn et al., 2017; Krohn et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jinn et al., 2019; Jinn et al., 2017; Krohn et al., 2020.

claim: Loss of TMEM175 function can lead to increased susceptibility to α-synuclein cytotoxicity.
source: Loss of TMEM175 function can lead to numerous defects in the endolysosomal system including dysregulation of lysosomal pH, defects in autophagy and mitophagy, reduced glucocerebrosidase activity, and an increased susceptibility to α-synuclein cytotoxicity (Jinn et al., 2019; Jinn et al., 2017; Krohn et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jinn et al., 2019; Jinn et al., 2017; Krohn et al., 2020.

claim: Point mutations in TMEM175 have been identified that are strongly associated with development of Parkinson's disease.
source: Dysregulation of lysosomal function is commonly associated with neurodegenerative disease and point mutations in TMEM175 have been identified that are strongly associated with development of Parkinson's disease (PD) (Blauwendraat et al., 2019; Iwaki et al., 2019; Jinn et al., 2019; Jinn et al., 2017; Krohn et al., 2020; Nalls et al., 2014; Wie et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The M393T point mutation is a loss-of-function mutation associated with increased likelihood and early onset of Parkinson's disease.
source: For example, the M393T point mutation is a loss-of-function mutation associated with the increased likelihood and early onset of PD and the Q65P mutant is a gain-of-function mutation associated with a reduced likelihood of developing of PD (Wie et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wie et al., 2021.

claim: The Q65P mutant is a gain-of-function mutation associated with a reduced likelihood of developing Parkinson's disease.
source: For example, the M393T point mutation is a loss-of-function mutation associated with the increased likelihood and early onset of PD and the Q65P mutant is a gain-of-function mutation associated with a reduced likelihood of developing of PD (Wie et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wie et al., 2021.

claim: TMEM175 channels from prokaryotes and humans adopt a unique architecture relative to all known ion channel structures.
source: Consistent with being evolutionarily distinct from other ion channels, TMEM175 channels from prokaryotes and humans adopt a unique architecture relative to all known ion channel structures (Brunner et al., 2020; Lee et al., 2017; Oh et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Brunner et al., 2020; Lee et al., 2017; Oh et al., 2020.

claim: Structures of two prokaryotic TMEM175 homologs in closed states revealed a homotetrameric channel possessing a central ion conduction pathway lined by several layers of hydrophobic residues from the first transmembrane helix of each of the four protomers.
source: Structures of two prokaryotic TMEM175 homologs in closed states revealed a homotetrameric channel possessing a central ion conduction pathway lined by several layers of hydrophobic residues from the first transmembrane (TM) helix of each of the four protomers (Brunner et al., 2020; Lee et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Brunner et al., 2020; Lee et al., 2017.

claim: Human TMEM175 channels are homodimers, rather than homotetramers.
source: However, human TMEM175 (hTMEM175) channels are homodimers, rather than homotetramers, and are ~30-fold selective for K+ over Na+, whereas prokaryotic TMEM175 channels exhibit only 2- to 4-fold selectivity for K+/Na+ (Cang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cang et al., 2015.

claim: Human TMEM175 channels are ~30-fold selective for K+ over Na+.
source: However, human TMEM175 (hTMEM175) channels are homodimers, rather than homotetramers, and are ~30-fold selective for K+ over Na+, whereas prokaryotic TMEM175 channels exhibit only 2- to 4-fold selectivity for K+/Na+ (Cang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cang et al., 2015.

claim: Prokaryotic TMEM175 channels exhibit only 2- to 4-fold selectivity for K+/Na+.
source: However, human TMEM175 (hTMEM175) channels are homodimers, rather than homotetramers, and are ~30-fold selective for K+ over Na+, whereas prokaryotic TMEM175 channels exhibit only 2- to 4-fold selectivity for K+/Na+ (Cang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cang et al., 2015.

claim: hTMEM175 protomers consist of two homologous repeats of six TM helices, which assemble into a dimer to form the channel.
source: hTMEM175 protomers consist of two homologous repeats of six TM helices, which assemble into a dimer to form the channel.
evidence: This is a structural description based on the authors' previous work (Oh et al., 2020).

claim: A 2-fold symmetric ion conduction pathway runs along the center of the dimer, lined by two copies of TM1 and TM7.
source: A 2-fold symmetric ion conduction pathway runs along the center of the dimer, lined by two copies of TM1 and TM7, the first helices of each repeat.
evidence: This is a structural description based on the authors' previous work (Oh et al., 2020).

claim: The pore of TMEM175 contains no clusters of hydrophilic side chains or backbone atoms that control selectivity.
source: Unlike most cation channels, including canonical K+ channels such as KcsA and Shaker, the pore of TMEM175 contains no clusters of hydrophilic side chains or backbone atoms that control selectivity (Doyle et al., 1998; Long et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Doyle et al., 1998; Long et al., 2005 for comparison with canonical K+ channels.

claim: The most striking feature in the pore of TMEM175 is a narrow hydrophobic constriction formed by the side chains of the conserved Ile46 from TM1 and the conserved Ile271 from TM7.
source: Rather, the most striking feature in the pore of TMEM175 is a narrow hydrophobic constriction formed by the side chains of the conserved Ile46 from TM1 and the conserved Ile271 from TM7, which we termed the isoleucine constriction (Oh et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the authors' previous work (Oh et al., 2020).

claim: The resolution of the putative open state improved from 2.64 to 2.45 Å.
source: The resolution of the putative open state improved from 2.64 to 2.45 Å and the closed state improved from 3.03 to 2.61 Å (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Appendix 1—table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from reprocessing cryo-EM images and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The resolution of the closed state improved from 3.03 to 2.61 Å.
source: The resolution of the putative open state improved from 2.64 to 2.45 Å and the closed state improved from 3.03 to 2.61 Å (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Appendix 1—table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from reprocessing cryo-EM images and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The improved structures have an all-atom RMSD of 0.3 Å for the open state and 0.4 Å for the closed state compared to previously determined structures.
source: While the improved structures are similar to those previously determined with an all-atom RMSD of 0.3 Å for the open state and 0.4 Å for the closed state, the higher-resolution reconstructions allowed us to better define the ion conduction pathways (Figure 1A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison data.

claim: In both open and closed states, the ion conduction pathway is 2-fold symmetric, narrow, and largely devoid of polar contacts.
source: In both states, the ion conduction pathway is 2-fold symmetric, narrow, and largely devoid of polar contacts, particularly near the center due to the presence of several hydrophobic side chains including Ile46, Val50, Leu53, Ile271, Leu275, and Leu278 (Figure 1C–D).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the improved cryo-EM structures shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: In the closed state, the isoleucine constriction is too narrow to allow ion permeation.
source: In the closed state, the isoleucine constriction formed by Ile46 and Ile271 is too narrow to allow ion permeation (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the closed state structure shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In the closed state, the side chains of Ile271 point toward the channel axis, narrowing the pore to a minimum radius of 0.2 Å.
source: The side chains of Ile271 point toward the channel axis, narrowing the pore to a minimum radius of 0.2 Å (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is a structural measurement from the closed state structure shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: In the open state, conformational changes in the pore-lining helices TM1 and TM7 dilate the isoleucine constriction to a minimum radius of 1.6 Å.
source: In the open state, by contrast, conformational changes in the pore-lining helices TM1 and TM7 helices dilate the isoleucine constriction to a minimum radius of 1.6 Å, which appears to be sufficient to accommodate a partially dehydrated K+ ion (Figure 1C and E).
evidence: This is a structural measurement from the open state structure shown in Figure 1C and E.

claim: In the dilated conformation, the isoleucine constriction adopts a pseudo 4-fold symmetric configuration with the side chains of both Ile46 and Ile271 adopting the mt rotamer.
source: In its dilated conformation, the isoleucine constriction adopts a pseudo 4-fold symmetric configuration with the side chains of both Ile46 and Ile271 adopting the mt rotamer (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the open state structure shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Five ion-binding sites, called K1 through K5, and ordered water molecules were modeled in the pore of the open state.
source: The higher-resolution reconstructions also allowed an improved modeling of five ion-binding sites, which we call K1 through K5, and ordered water molecules in the pore of the open state.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the improved open state structure.

claim: Two non-protein densities are resolved at the K3 and K4 sites that flank the isoleucine constriction.
source: Two non-protein densities are now resolved at the K3 and K4 sites that flank the isoleucine constriction (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the improved open state structure shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The densities at K3 and K4 sites were assigned as K+ ions based on comparison with a structure determined in the presence of Cs+.
source: We assigned these densities as K+ ions based on our previous comparison with a structure determined in the presence of Cs+ (Oh et al., 2020).
evidence: This assignment is based on previous experimental comparison with Cs+ (Oh et al., 2020).

claim: The K3 and K4 ion-binding sites are positioned 3.7–4.0 Å away from the side chains of Ile46 and Ile271.
source: The K3 and K4 ion-binding sites are positioned 3.7–4.0 Å away from the side chains of Ile46 and Ile271 and are coordinated exclusively by water molecules (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a structural measurement from the open state structure shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ions in the K3 and K4 sites are only partially hydrated.
source: Notably, the ions in the K3 and K4 sites are only partially hydrated.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the open state structure.

claim: The K3-binding site is coordinated by four ordered water molecules that are between 2.8 and 3.0 Å away.
source: The K3-binding site on the cytoplasmic site of the constriction is coordinated by four ordered water molecules that are between 2.8 and 3.0 Å away, while the K4 site on the luminal side is coordinated by four water molecules that are between 2.9 and 3.5 Å away.
evidence: This is a structural measurement from the open state structure.

claim: The K4 site is coordinated by four water molecules that are between 2.9 and 3.5 Å away.
source: The K3-binding site on the cytoplasmic site of the constriction is coordinated by four ordered water molecules that are between 2.8 and 3.0 Å away, while the K4 site on the luminal side is coordinated by four water molecules that are between 2.9 and 3.5 Å away.
evidence: This is a structural measurement from the open state structure.

claim: The distance between the K3 and K4 sites is 2.8 Å and thus they are unlikely to be simultaneously occupied by ions.
source: The distance between the two sites is 2.8 Å and thus they are unlikely to be simultaneously occupied by ions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural measurement of the distance between K3 and K4 sites.

claim: For the closed state, three ion-binding sites and 25 water molecules were modeled into non-protein densities.
source: For the closed state, we can now model three ion-binding sites and 25 water molecules into non-protein densities (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the improved closed state structure shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In the cytosolic region of the pore, the K1 and K2 ion-binding sites and water molecules occupy almost identical positions in open and closed states.
source: In the cytosolic region of the pore, where the channel undergoes minimal conformational changes during gating, the K1 and K2 ion-binding sites and water molecules occupy almost identical positions to those resolved in the open state (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a structural comparison between open and closed states shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: K+ ions reach the isoleucine constriction readily from either side of the membrane, through a series of shallow free-energy barriers and transient-binding sites.
source: We observe that K+ ions reach the isoleucine constriction readily from either side of the membrane, through a series of shallow free-energy barriers and transient-binding sites (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an observation from MD simulations shown in Figure 2A.

claim: At the isoleucine constriction, the free energy increases steeply, peaking at about 7 kcal/mol for K+.
source: At the isoleucine constriction, however, the free energy increases steeply, peaking at about 7 kcal/mol (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The simulation data reveals no evidence of a multi-ion process involving concurrent occupancy of proximal-binding sites near the constriction.
source: Unlike in canonical K+ channels, however, the simulation data reveals no evidence of a multi-ion process involving concurrent occupancy of proximal-binding sites near the constriction (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an observation from MD simulations shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: K+ ions approach and cross the isoleucine constriction individually.
source: Instead, K+ ions approach and cross this constriction individually.
evidence: This is an observation from MD simulations.

claim: K+ permeation requires a gradual but drastic depletion of the ion hydration shells.
source: It is apparent, too, that permeation requires a gradual but drastic depletion of the ion hydration shells.
evidence: This is an observation from MD simulations.

claim: As K+ traverses the isoleucine constriction, the first two hydration shells are reduced to only ~9 molecules, down from 31 in the bulk.
source: As K+ traverses the isoleucine constriction, the first two hydration shells are reduced to only ~9 molecules, down from 31 in the bulk; the first shell averages to about 4, down from 7 (Figures 2B, C ,, 3A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from MD simulations shown in Figures 2B, C, and 3A.

claim: The first hydration shell of K+ averages to about 4 molecules at the constriction, down from 7 in bulk.
source: As K+ traverses the isoleucine constriction, the first two hydration shells are reduced to only ~9 molecules, down from 31 in the bulk; the first shell averages to about 4, down from 7 (Figures 2B, C ,, 3A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from MD simulations shown in Figures 2B, C, and 3A.

claim: Acidic side chains at both the luminal and cytosolic entrances of the pore generate a strongly favorable electrostatic field that spans the length of the pore.
source: Indeed, further examination of the simulated trajectories using Poisson theory (Materials and methods) reveals that acidic side chains at both the luminal and cytosolic entrances of the pore generate a strongly favorable electrostatic field that spans the length of the pore (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a result from analysis of MD simulations using Poisson theory, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Integration of the potential-of-mean-force profile obtained at 0 mV and 100 mM KCl translates into a single-channel conductance of approximately 0.23 pS.
source: Integration of the potential-of-mean-force profile obtained at 0 mV and 100 mM KCl translates into a single-channel conductance of approximately 0.23 pS (Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a calculated result from the MD simulation data.

claim: At 500 mV, the calculated conductance would produce a 0.1 pA current, or a rate of K+ permeation of about 0.6 ions/μs.
source: At 500 mV, and assuming the structure of the channel is completely unresponsive to voltage, this conductance would in turn produce a 0.1 pA current, or a rate of K+ permeation of about 0.6 ions/μs.
evidence: This is a calculated result based on the conductance estimate from MD simulations.

claim: A 1-μs-long MD simulation at 500 mV and 400 mM KCl revealed two K+ permeation events.
source: This trajectory revealed a stable pore conformation and two K+ permeation events, confirming that the open state is functionally conductive and validating the single-ion mechanism inferred from the free-energy simulations (Figure 3C and D; Figure 3—video 1 and Figure 3—video 2).
evidence: This is a result from a conventional MD simulation shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The conventional MD simulation at 500 mV confirms that the open state is functionally conductive.
source: This trajectory revealed a stable pore conformation and two K+ permeation events, confirming that the open state is functionally conductive and validating the single-ion mechanism inferred from the free-energy simulations (Figure 3C and D; Figure 3—video 1 and Figure 3—video 2).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the conventional MD simulation shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The free-energy barrier at the isoleucine constriction peaks at about 8 kcal/mol for Na+ compared to about 7 kcal/mol for K+.
source: The largest difference between the profiles is the magnitude of the barrier at the isoleucine constriction, which peaks at about 8 kcal/mol relative to bulk for Na+ compared to about 7 kcal/mol for K+.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from MD simulations comparing K+ and Na+.

claim: Integration of the potential-of-mean-force profile obtained for Na+ translates into a single-channel conductance of approximately 0.037 pS.
source: Integration of the potential-of-mean-force profile obtained for Na+ translates into a single-channel conductance of approximately 0.037 pS, that is, the calculated conductance for Na+ is 6-fold smaller than for K+.
evidence: This is a calculated result from the MD simulation data for Na+.

claim: The calculated conductance for Na+ is 6-fold smaller than for K+.
source: Integration of the potential-of-mean-force profile obtained for Na+ translates into a single-channel conductance of approximately 0.037 pS, that is, the calculated conductance for Na+ is 6-fold smaller than for K+.
evidence: This is a calculated result from the MD simulation data comparing K+ and Na+.

claim: Na+ permeation proceeds via a single-ion mechanism.
source: As observed for K+, Na+ permeation proceeds via a single-ion mechanism (Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an observation from MD simulations shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Figure 3B.

claim: The degree of dehydration required for permeation differs between K+ and Na+.
source: By contrast, the degree of dehydration required for permeation clearly differs.
evidence: This is an observation from MD simulations comparing K+ and Na+.

claim: The depletion in both the first and second solvation shells, relative to bulk numbers, is significantly smaller for Na+ than for K+.
source: We observe that the depletion in the both the first and second solvation shells, relative to bulk numbers, is significantly smaller for Na+ than for K+.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from MD simulations comparing K+ and Na+.

claim: Mutating both Ile46 and Ile271 to asparagine diminishes the selectivity of TMEM175.
source: It was previously demonstrated that mutating both Ile46 and Ile271 to asparagine diminishes the selectivity of TMEM175, indicating that the hydrophobicity of the isoleucine constriction is crucial for selectivity (Lee et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2017.

claim: The hydrophobicity of the isoleucine constriction is crucial for selectivity.
source: It was previously demonstrated that mutating both Ile46 and Ile271 to asparagine diminishes the selectivity of TMEM175, indicating that the hydrophobicity of the isoleucine constriction is crucial for selectivity (Lee et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference from the mutagenesis result cited from Lee et al., 2017.

claim: The exchange of a K+ ion at the isoleucine constriction with a Na+ ion results in a free-energy gain in wild-type TMEM175.
source: In both cases the exchange results in a free-energy gain (Figure 4A), consistent with the notion that Na+ is the favored species at the constriction.
evidence: This is a result from MD/FEP simulations shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Na+ is the favored species at the isoleucine constriction.
source: In both cases the exchange results in a free-energy gain (Figure 4A), consistent with the notion that Na+ is the favored species at the constriction.
evidence: This is an inference from the MD/FEP simulation results shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The free-energy gain for Na+ at the constriction is smaller than that observed for the exchange in bulk water.
source: However, this gain is smaller than that observed for the exchange of a K+ ion in bulk water with a Na+ ion.
evidence: This is a result from MD/FEP simulations comparing the constriction to bulk water.

claim: The differential relative to bulk is 1.2 kcal/mol in favor of K+ for wild-type TMEM175.
source: Specifically, the differential relative to bulk is 1.2 kcal/mol in favor of K+, similar to the ~1 kcal/mol difference in the peak values of the free-energy curves discussed in the previous section (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a calculated result from MD/FEP simulations.

claim: The I46V mutant is about 2.5-fold (or 0.5 kcal/mol) less K+-selective than the wild-type channel.
source: Na+ is however favored to a larger extent in the I46V mutant, whose isoleucine constriction has a similar hydrophobicity but is expanded by the loss of a methyl group from the side chain of Ile46 in each protomer (Figure 4A); specifically, the calculations indicate that this mutant is about 2.5-fold (or 0.5 kcal/mol) less K+-selective than the wild-type channel (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a calculated result from MD/FEP simulations shown in Figure 4A.

claim: I46V and I271V displayed Cs+-selective currents with Erev of –13 and –16 mV, corresponding to PCs/Na of 1.7 and 1.9, respectively.
source: Following AP-6 background subtraction, I46V and I271V displayed Cs+-selective currents with Erev of –13 and –16 mV, corresponding to Cs+ over Na+ permeability ratios (PCs/Na) of 1.7 and 1.9, respectively (Figure 5).
evidence: This is an experimental result from whole-cell patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 5.

claim: The PCs/Na of wild-type TMEM175 is estimated to be 20 (Erev of –76 mV).
source: Using the same background subtraction approach, we estimated the PCs/Na of wild-type TMEM175 to be 20 (Erev of –76 mV).
evidence: This is an experimental result from whole-cell patch clamp recordings.

claim: There is a 10-fold reduction in PCs/Na ion permeation ratio for I46V and I271V compared to wild-type TMEM175.
source: This 10-fold reduction in PCs/Na ion permeation ratio is in line with the computational analyses of the free-energy difference in resulting from K+ to Na+ ion exchange at the isoleucine constriction of I46V and wild type.
evidence: This is a comparison between experimental and computational results.

claim: Increasing the size of the isoleucine constriction leads to a clear reduction in K+ selectivity.
source: These data demonstrate that increasing the size of the isoleucine constriction leads to a clear reduction in K+ selectivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental mutagenesis results.

claim: The isoleucine constriction is universally conserved among eukaryotic TMEM175 channels.
source: Thus, the isoleucine constriction, which is universally conserved among eukaryotic TMEM175 channels, serves as a hydrophobic selectivity filter that is exquisitely sensitive to very subtle changes in its structure.
evidence: This is a statement about sequence conservation.

claim: The isoleucine constriction serves as a hydrophobic selectivity filter that is exquisitely sensitive to very subtle changes in its structure.
source: Thus, the isoleucine constriction, which is universally conserved among eukaryotic TMEM175 channels, serves as a hydrophobic selectivity filter that is exquisitely sensitive to very subtle changes in its structure.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the combined experimental and computational results.

claim: In canonical K+ channels, backbone and side chain oxygen atoms provide a series of direct coordinating interactions that closely resemble those experienced by the ion in bulk water.
source: In canonical K+ channels, backbone and side chain oxygen atoms provide a series of direct coordinating interactions that closely resemble those experienced by the ion in bulk water.
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanism of canonical K+ channels based on established knowledge.

claim: In canonical K+ channels, the cost of dehydration is almost entirely offset by channel-ion and ion-ion interactions.
source: Thus, the cost of dehydration is almost entirely offset by channel-ion and ion-ion interactions, and the resulting free-energy barriers for permeation are small.
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanism of canonical K+ channels based on established knowledge.

claim: Direct protein-ion interactions are lacking for much of the TMEM175 pore, and entirely absent near the isoleucine constriction.
source: In contrast, such interactions are lacking for much of the TMEM175 pore, and entirely absent near the isoleucine constriction.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM structures and MD simulations.

claim: K+ ions crossing the TMEM175 pore must shed much of their hydration shells, with only ~9 of the 31 water molecules in the first two shells remaining at the constriction.
source: K+ ions crossing the pore must nevertheless shed much of their hydration shells; only ~9 of the 31 water molecules in its first two shells remain at the constriction.
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations.

claim: Ions permeate TMEM175 one at a time, without direct or indirect knock-on interactions.
source: In addition, ions permeate TMEM175 one at a time, without direct or indirect knock-on interactions.
evidence: This is an observation from MD simulations.

claim: Permeation is strongly favored by a delocalized electrostatic field across the pore, which offsets much of the cost of ion dehydration, resulting in a free-energy barrier of ~7 kcal/mol.
source: Permeation is however strongly favored by a delocalized electrostatic field across the pore, which offsets much of the cost of ion dehydration, resulting in a free-energy barrier of ~7 kcal/mol (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations and Poisson theory analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: The unitary conductance of hTMEM175 is estimated to be 0.1–0.5 pS.
source: Indeed, considering that MD simulations using conventional force fields tend to underestimate ion conduction rates, in some cases up to 10-fold (Allen et al., 2006; Mironenko et al., 2021), we estimate the unitary conductance of hTMEM175 is 0.1–0.5 pS, which is well within the broad range of experimentally measured permeation rates for other selective cation channels such as ~100 pS for Slo K+ and 9–24 fS for CRAC channels (Tao et al., 2016; Zweifach and Lewis, 1993).
evidence: This is an estimate based on MD simulation results and comparison with literature values for other channels.

claim: The balance between protein-ion interactions and solvent-ion interactions is dependent on the ion type.
source: Importantly, the balance between protein-ion interactions and solvent-ion interactions is dependent on the ion type, and so these opposing forces also govern ion selectivity in channels.
evidence: This is a general principle about ion selectivity in channels.

claim: Dehydration of Na+ is much more costly than that of K+, with the penalty for full dehydration being ~18 kcal/mol greater.
source: For example, when rationalizing differences in permeability between K+ and Na+, it is useful to keep in mind that dehydration of Na+ is much more costly than that of K+; the penalty for full dehydration is ~18 kcal/mol greater, rendering it a trillion-fold less probable.
evidence: This is a statement about the thermodynamics of ion dehydration based on established knowledge.

claim: The observed selectivity of biological K+ channels against Na+ is only 1000-fold or less.
source: However, the observed selectivity of biological K+ channels against Na+ is only 1000-fold or less, implying Na+ establishes much more favorable interactions with the selectivity filters of this kind of K+ channels, as noted in previous studies (Kim and Allen, 2011; Kopec et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement about the selectivity of K+ channels based on established knowledge and citations.

claim: For TMEM175, favorable protein-ion interactions are imparted by residues near the luminal and cytoplasmic entrances to the pore, quite far from the isoleucine constriction.
source: Remarkably, for TMEM175 these favorable protein-ion interactions are imparted by residues near the luminal and cytoplasmic entrances to the pore, quite far from the isoleucine constriction.
evidence: This is an observation from MD simulations and Poisson theory analysis.

claim: The ion selectivity of TMEM175 primarily results from a differential in the degree of dehydration required for permeation, relative to bulk water.
source: Thus, we propose that the ion selectivity of TMEM175 primarily results from a differential in the degree of dehydration required for permeation, relative to bulk water.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the combined results from MD simulations and experiments.

claim: The large conductance Slo1 K+ channel has been observed in lysosomes.
